questions.explanation:
### Explanation
In **Genesis 37:11**, it states that Joseph's brothers were **jealous** of him because of his dreams and the special coat their father Jacob had given him.

questions.question: Which epistle emphasizes that 'God is love'?
questions.explanation:
### Explanation
In **1 John 4:8** and **1 John 4:16**, the writer declares: 'Anyone who does not love does not know God, because **God is love**.'

questions.question: What was the initial sign of the covenant between God and Abraham according to Genesis 17?
questions.explanation: In **Genesis 17**, God established circumcision as the perpetual sign of the covenant between Him and Abraham and his descendants. Every male in their household was required to be circumcised as an outward mark of their dedication to the covenant.

questions.question: Which specific judicial case first demonstrated Solomon's God-given wisdom to the people of Israel?

options.A: The dividing of the inheritance of Naboth
options.B: The dispute between two harlots over a living child
options.C: The taxation dispute with the tribe of Ephraim
options.D: The treaty negotiation with Hiram of Tyre

questions.explanation: Found in **1 Kings 3:16-28**, Solomon's verdict regarding the two mothers claiming the same living child revealed his profound insight. By ordering the child to be cut in two, he identified the true mother by her willingness to give up the child to save its life.

questions.question: How many times did the Lord call Samuel before Eli realized it was God speaking?
questions.explanation: According to **1 Samuel 3:1-10**, the Lord called Samuel three times. Each time, Samuel ran to Eli thinking Eli had called him. It was only after the third time that Eli perceived that the Lord was calling the boy.

questions.question: Amos prophesied against Israel primarily because of which social evil?

options.A: Their failure to build the Temple
options.B: Their oppression of the poor and perversion of justice
options.D: The lack of animal sacrifices in the high places

questions.explanation: Amos was a prophet of social justice. He condemned the wealthy elite for trampling the needy, selling the righteous for silver, and turning justice into wormwood (**Amos 5:7, 5:12**). He emphasized that ritual worship is meaningless without righteousness.

questions.question: What did Hosea’s marriage to Gomer symbolize to the people of Israel?

options.C: God's unconditional, forgiving love for unfaithful Israel
options.D: The danger of marrying foreign women

questions.explanation: Hosea's marriage to Gomer, an unfaithful wife, served as a prophetic metaphor for Israel's unfaithfulness to God through idolatry. Despite Israel's 'adultery' (worshipping Baal), God promised to restore them, mirroring Hosea's persistence in seeking his wife (**Hosea 1-3**).

questions.question: Who was chosen to replace Judas Iscariot as an apostle?
questions.explanation: In **Acts 1:23-26**, after praying and casting lots, the apostles selected Matthias to replace Judas Iscariot, ensuring the number of the twelve apostles was complete before the coming of the Holy Spirit.

questions.question: In the Parable of the Sower, what does the 'seed' represent?

options.B: The message of the Kingdom of God

questions.explanation: Jesus explicitly explains in **Luke 8:11** (and parallel passages in Matthew and Mark) that the 'seed is the word of God.' The different types of soil represent the varying levels of human receptivity to the message.

questions.question: According to the Epistle of James, what is the relationship between faith and works?

options.A: Faith is sufficient; works are unnecessary
options.B: Works are sufficient; faith is unnecessary
options.D: Works are only for the apostles

questions.explanation: James 2:17 states, 'So also faith, if it has no works, is dead by itself.' The Epistle emphasizes that genuine faith must manifest itself through tangible actions of love and obedience to God.

questions.question: What message did Jeremiah convey regarding 'individual responsibility' in his prophecy?

options.A: The entire nation must suffer for the sins of the King
options.B: Every person is responsible for their own sin before God
options.C: Prophets bear the burden of the sins of the people
options.D: Children are always punished for their father's sins

questions.explanation: Jeremiah (and Ezekiel) shifted the focus from collective guilt to individual responsibility. **Jeremiah 31:29-30** states that everyone will die for their own sin: 'Every one who eats sour grapes his teeth shall be set on edge'—meaning each individual is accountable for their own actions.

questions.question: Which scripture did Jesus use to resist the devil when tempted to jump from the pinnacle of the temple?

options.B: You shall not put the Lord your God to the test
options.C: Man shall not live by bread alone
options.D: Worship the Lord your God and serve him only

questions.explanation: In **Matthew 4:7**, when the devil tempted Jesus to jump to prove his identity, Jesus quoted Deuteronomy 6:16: 'You shall not put the Lord your God to the test,' demonstrating his trust in the Father's timing and will.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 12, what does Paul identify as the 'greatest' spiritual gift that the church should pursue?
questions.explanation: In **1 Corinthians 13**, often called the 'Love Chapter,' Paul explicitly states that while other gifts are temporary, love remains the greatest and most enduring of all spiritual virtues, foundational for the proper exercise of all other gifts.

questions.question: Where did the contest between Elijah and the prophets of Baal take place?
questions.explanation: The dramatic showdown where Elijah proved that Yahweh is the true God by consuming the sacrifice with fire occurred on **Mount Carmel** (1 Kings 18:19-40).

questions.question: Who was the man that God sent to restore Saul's sight in Damascus?
questions.explanation: According to **Acts 9:10-18**, Ananias was a disciple in Damascus who, though afraid, obeyed God's instruction to find Saul and pray for him, resulting in the scales falling from Saul's eyes.

questions.question: How does 1 Peter instruct Christians to react when they suffer for the name of Christ?
questions.explanation: **1 Peter 4:13-14** encourages believers to rejoice insofar as they share Christ's sufferings, assuring them that the Spirit of glory rests upon them when they are insulted for the name of Christ.

questions.question: What was Nehemiah’s primary occupation while in the service of King Artaxerxes?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah served as the **cupbearer** to King Artaxerxes of Persia. This was a position of high trust, as the cupbearer ensured the king's drink was not poisoned, granting Nehemiah regular access to the King.

questions.question: In the Parable of the Unforgiving Servant, why did the master get angry with the servant?

options.B: Because the servant did not forgive a fellow servant his small debt
options.C: Because the servant stole from the royal treasury
options.D: Because the servant insulted the master's son

questions.explanation: Found in **Matthew 18:21-35**, the lesson of the parable is that God's forgiveness towards us should compel us to forgive others. The servant was condemned because he demanded payment from his fellow servant after having been forgiven a much larger debt himself.

questions.question: In Romans 13, how does Paul define the Christian's obligation to the state?

options.C: Submission to authorities as they are instituted by God
options.D: Complete withdrawal from all civil government

questions.explanation: **Romans 13:1-7** teaches that government authorities are instituted by God for the maintenance of order. Therefore, believers are expected to obey the laws of the land as long as they do not contradict the supreme law of God.

questions.question: Which prophet confronted King David after his affair with Bathsheba?
questions.explanation: The prophet **Nathan** delivered the famous parable of the rich man and the poor man's lamb to confront David regarding his sin with Bathsheba and his orchestration of Uriah's death (**2 Samuel 12**).

questions.question: In the Parable of the Good Samaritan, who was the first person to ignore the wounded man on the road?
questions.explanation: According to **Luke 10:31**, a priest was traveling down the road, saw the man who had been beaten by robbers, and passed by on the other side, failing to show mercy.

questions.question: What piece of armor in the 'Full Armor of God' is used to deflect the flaming darts of the evil one?
questions.explanation: In **Ephesians 6:16**, Paul explains that the Shield of Faith is essential to 'extinguish all the flaming darts of the evil one.' It is the active trust in God's promises that protects the believer.

questions.question: What did God use to get Moses' attention at the beginning of his call?
questions.explanation: In **Exodus 3:2**, God appeared to Moses in the wilderness of Horeb through a bush that was burning with fire yet was not consumed, signaling the beginning of his mission to lead the Israelites out of Egypt.

questions.question: Which disciple denied Jesus three times before the cock crowed?
questions.explanation: All four gospels record **Peter's** threefold denial of Jesus on the night of His arrest, fulfilling Jesus' earlier prediction that Peter would deny Him before the rooster crowed.

questions.question: What does Paul suggest should 'dwell in you richly' in Colossians 3:16?
questions.explanation: **Colossians 3:16** exhorts believers: 'Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly, teaching and admonishing one another in all wisdom, singing psalms and hymns and spiritual songs with thankfulness in your hearts to God.'

questions.question: What was the first city captured by the Israelites after crossing the Jordan River?
questions.explanation: As recorded in **Joshua 6**, the walls of **Jericho** fell after the Israelites marched around the city for seven days, making it the first major victory in the conquest of Canaan.

questions.question: According to the Beatitudes, who shall see God?
questions.explanation: In **Matthew 5:8**, Jesus declares, 'Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.' This emphasizes that spiritual vision and relationship with God are tied to moral and internal purity.

questions.question: What was the name of the runaway slave Paul sent back to his master?
questions.explanation: The Epistle to **Philemon** is a personal letter from Paul to Philemon, asking him to receive back his runaway slave, Onesimus, not as a slave, but as a beloved brother in Christ.

questions.question: Why was Daniel thrown into the lions' den?

options.B: He prayed to his God despite the King’s decree
options.C: He broke the idols of Babylon

questions.explanation: In **Daniel 6**, Daniel continued to pray to the God of Israel three times a day, defying King Darius's decree that forbade prayer to anyone other than the King for thirty days.

questions.question: Who was the first person to see the resurrected Jesus according to the Gospel accounts?
questions.explanation: According to **John 20:11-18** (and consistent with other accounts), Jesus first appeared to Mary Magdalene at the tomb after His resurrection, commissioning her to tell the disciples.

questions.question: How did Paul describe his life’s journey in his final letter, 2 Timothy?

options.A: I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race
options.B: I have gained much wealth for the Lord

questions.explanation: In **2 Timothy 4:7**, Paul reflects on his life of service and suffering, stating, 'I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith,' signaling his readiness for his imminent death.

questions.question: What was the immediate consequence of Adam and Eve eating the forbidden fruit?

options.B: They recognized their nakedness and hid
options.D: They were made rulers of the beasts

questions.explanation: In **Genesis 3:7**, immediately after eating the fruit, the eyes of both were opened, and they realized they were naked; they sewed fig leaves together and hid themselves from the presence of the Lord among the trees.

questions.question: Which of the following phrases best describes God's action on the seventh day of creation?

options.C: He created the sun and moon

questions.explanation: According to **Genesis 2:2-3**, after God completed His work of creation in six days, He rested on the seventh day and sanctified it, establishing the principle of the Sabbath.

questions.question: What was the immediate consequence of Adam and Eve's disobedience in the Garden of Eden?

options.B: They realized their nakedness and hid

questions.explanation: In **Genesis 3:7**, upon eating the forbidden fruit, the eyes of both were opened, and they realized they were naked. They sewed fig leaves together and hid themselves from the presence of the Lord among the trees.

questions.question: Why did Joseph refuse the advances of Potiphar's wife?

options.C: He considered it a sin against God

questions.explanation: In **Genesis 39:9**, Joseph explicitly stated that he could not commit such a great wickedness and sin against God, demonstrating his moral integrity and fear of the Lord.

questions.question: Who finally instructed Samuel on how to respond to God's call?
questions.explanation: In **1 Samuel 3:8-9**, Eli, the priest, realized that the Lord was calling the boy and instructed Samuel to say, 'Speak, Lord, for your servant hears.'

questions.question: Where did Jeroboam set up golden calves to prevent people from going to Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: As recorded in **1 Kings 12:28-29**, Jeroboam set up two golden calves in Bethel and Dan to discourage the Israelites from traveling to Jerusalem to worship, fearing they would return to the house of David.

questions.topic: Elijah and the Prophets of Baal
questions.question: How did the prophets of Baal try to get their god to answer them on Mount Carmel?

options.C: They cut themselves with swords and lances

questions.explanation: In **1 Kings 18:28**, the prophets of Baal cried aloud and cut themselves after their custom with swords and lances until the blood gushed out upon them, in a desperate attempt to gain Baal's attention.

questions.question: Amos criticized the wealthy in Israel primarily for which of the following?

options.A: Refusing to sacrifice at the temple

questions.explanation: The book of **Amos (e.g., Amos 5:12)** highlights the prophet's condemnation of the wealthy who 'trample the head of the poor' and deny justice to the needy in the gates.

questions.question: What touched Isaiah’s lips to purge his sin during his vision of the Lord?
questions.explanation: In **Isaiah 6:6-7**, a seraph flew to Isaiah having in his hand a burning coal which he had taken with tongs from the altar and touched his mouth, saying, 'Your guilt is taken away.'

questions.question: According to Isaiah 53, how did the Servant react to his oppression?

options.C: He opened not his mouth like a lamb led to slaughter
options.D: He cursed those who hurt him

questions.explanation: In **Isaiah 53:7**, the prophet writes that the servant was oppressed and afflicted, yet he opened not his mouth, likened to a lamb that is led to the slaughter.

questions.question: What did the voice from heaven say at the baptism of Jesus?

options.A: This is my beloved son in whom I am well pleased
options.C: Repent for the kingdom is at hand
options.D: This is a great prophet of Israel

questions.explanation: According to **Matthew 3:17** (and parallel passages in Mark and Luke), the voice from heaven declared, 'This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.'

questions.question: How did Jesus counter the devil's temptation to turn stones into bread?

options.B: By fasting for another forty days
options.C: By quoting the Scripture from Deuteronomy

questions.explanation: In **Matthew 4:4**, Jesus responded to the tempter by saying, 'It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God,' quoting **Deuteronomy 8:3**.

questions.question: In the parable of the Sower, what does the seed that fell on rocky ground represent?

options.A: Those who hear the word and immediately reject it
options.B: Those who receive the word with joy but have no root
options.C: Those who are choked by the cares of the world

questions.explanation: According to **Matthew 13:20-21**, the seed on rocky ground represents individuals who hear the word and receive it with joy, but have no root in themselves and fall away when persecution arises.

questions.question: Which two Old Testament figures appeared with Jesus on the mount of Transfiguration?
questions.explanation: In the Synoptic accounts (**Matthew 17, Mark 9, Luke 9**), Moses (representing the Law) and Elijah (representing the Prophets) appeared and talked with Jesus about his departure.

questions.question: Jesus entered Jerusalem riding on which animal?
questions.explanation: The Triumphal Entry is recorded in **Matthew 21:1-11** (and parallels). Jesus instructed his disciples to bring a colt, the foal of a donkey, to fulfill the prophecy of Zechariah 9:9.

questions.question: In the Great Commission (Matthew 28:19), what were the disciples commanded to do?

options.A: Stay in Jerusalem to wait for the Spirit

questions.explanation: The Great Commission in **Matthew 28:19** explicitly commands the disciples: 'Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.'

questions.question: Who was chosen to replace Judas Iscariot among the twelve apostles?
questions.explanation: In **Acts 1:23-26**, after praying and casting lots between Joseph called Barsabbas and Matthias, the lot fell on Matthias, and he was added to the eleven apostles.

questions.topic: The Coming of the Holy Spirit
questions.question: On which festival did the Holy Spirit descend upon the apostles?
questions.explanation: **Acts 2:1** states: 'When the day of Pentecost had come, they were all together in one place,' and the Holy Spirit filled them, enabling them to speak in other tongues.

questions.question: What did Stephen say while being stoned, echoing the words of Jesus?

options.A: Into thy hands I commit my spirit
options.B: Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do
options.C: Lord, do not hold this sin against them
options.D: My God, why have you forsaken me?

questions.explanation: In **Acts 7:60**, as Stephen was dying, he fell on his knees and cried out with a loud voice, 'Lord, do not hold this sin against them,' mirroring Jesus' words on the cross.

questions.question: Where was Saul going when he encountered the risen Christ?
questions.explanation: According to **Acts 9:1-3**, Saul was on his way to Damascus with letters of authority to persecute Christians when a light from heaven flashed around him.

questions.question: What was the main outcome of the Jerusalem Council in Acts 15?

options.A: Gentiles must be circumcised to be saved
options.B: Gentile converts do not need to observe the Mosaic law of circumcision
options.C: All Christians must move to Jerusalem
options.D: Paul was removed from the apostleship

questions.explanation: In **Acts 15:19-20**, James concluded that they should not trouble the Gentiles who turn to God, requiring them only to abstain from things polluted by idols, sexual immorality, things strangled, and blood.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 13, which of these is NOT stated about love?
questions.explanation: In **1 Corinthians 13:4**, Paul explicitly writes that 'love is patient and kind; love does not envy or boast; it is not arrogant.'

questions.question: What does Paul instruct the Colossians to 'put on' as God’s chosen people?

options.B: Compassionate hearts, kindness, humility, and patience

questions.explanation: In **Colossians 3:12**, Paul writes, 'Put on then, as God's chosen ones, holy and beloved, compassionate hearts, kindness, humility, meekness, and patience.'

questions.question: According to the Epistle of James, what is the nature of faith without works?
questions.explanation: In **James 2:17**, the writer concludes, 'So also faith by itself, if it does not have works, is dead.'

questions.question: Paul argues in Romans 3 that justification comes through what?
questions.explanation: In **Romans 3:22-24**, Paul clarifies that 'the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ for all who believe,' and that humanity is justified by His grace as a gift.

questions.question: Peter describes Christians as being what kind of people?

options.A: A chosen race and a royal priesthood
options.C: The elite of the Roman Empire

questions.explanation: In **1 Peter 2:9**, Peter writes, 'But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for his own possession.'

questions.question: According to 1 John 4, how do we know that we have passed from death to life?
questions.explanation: In **1 John 3:14**, the author states, 'We know that we have passed out of death into life, because we love the brothers. Whoever does not love abides in death.'

questions.question: Which of the following is listed as a fruit of the Spirit in Galatians 5:22-23?
questions.explanation: **Galatians 5:22-23** lists the fruit of the Spirit as: 'love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control.'

questions.question: Why does Peter encourage believers to be subject to every human institution?

options.A: To avoid being killed by the Romans
options.C: Because the government is always right

questions.explanation: In **1 Peter 2:13**, Peter instructs: 'Be subject for the Lord's sake to every human institution, whether it be to the emperor as supreme.'

questions.question: What does Paul say we should do instead of being anxious about anything?
questions.explanation: In **Philippians 4:6**, Paul says, 'Do not be anxious about anything, but in everything by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known to God.'

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 15, what does Paul argue would be the case if Christ had not been raised?

options.B: We would still be saved by the law
options.C: The apostles would still be celebrated
options.D: Christianity would be a branch of Judaism

questions.explanation: In **1 Corinthians 15:14**, Paul writes, 'And if Christ has not been raised, then our preaching is in vain and your faith is in vain.'

questions.question: Which of Jethro's pieces of advice to Moses centered on the principle of effective administration?

options.A: The need for a national census
options.B: The appointment of capable men to judge minor cases
options.C: The establishment of a permanent temple

questions.explanation: In Exodus 18, Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, observed that Moses was overburdened. He advised Moses to appoint 'capable men from all the people—men who fear God, trustworthy men who hate dishonest gain' to judge minor disputes, allowing Moses to focus on bringing major cases before God.

questions.question: What was the primary sign of the covenant between God and Noah that signified the end of the flood?

options.B: The setting of a rainbow in the clouds

questions.explanation: According to Genesis 9:13-17, God established a covenant with Noah and all living creatures that He would never again destroy the earth with a flood. The rainbow was established as the everlasting sign of this promise.

questions.question: How did God demonstrate His sovereignty during the crossing of the Red Sea?

options.A: By sending a plague upon the Egyptians
options.B: By causing a strong east wind to blow all night
options.C: By appearing as a burning bush
options.D: By ordering the people to fast for forty days

questions.explanation: In Exodus 14:21, the Bible records that the Lord caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all that night, making the sea dry land and dividing the waters for the Israelites to pass through.

questions.question: What was the occupation of Peter, Andrew, James, and John before Jesus called them?
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:18-22 describes Jesus calling Peter, Andrew, James, and John while they were by the Sea of Galilee mending their nets or fishing. He called them to become 'fishers of men'.

questions.question: In the Parable of the Sower, what does the 'seed sown among thorns' represent?

options.A: People who hear the word but are choked by life's worries and wealth
options.B: People who lack depth in their faith
options.C: People who do not understand the word
options.D: People who produce a hundredfold harvest

questions.explanation: According to Jesus' interpretation in Mark 4:18-19, the thorns represent the worries of this life, the deceitfulness of wealth, and the desires for other things, which choke the word and make it unfruitful.

questions.question: Who was the man compelled to carry the cross of Jesus on the way to Golgotha?
questions.explanation: As recorded in Mark 15:21, Luke 23:26, and Matthew 27:32, Simon of Cyrene, the father of Alexander and Rufus, was passing by on his way in from the country and was forced by the Roman soldiers to carry Jesus' cross.

questions.topic: Themes from the Acts of the Apostles
questions.question: What was the main criterion for choosing a replacement for Judas Iscariot?

options.A: He must be wealthy and influential
options.B: He must have been with the disciples from John's baptism to the ascension
options.C: He must have been a Pharisee
options.D: He must be a relative of Jesus

questions.explanation: In Acts 1:21-22, Peter established that the replacement for Judas had to be someone who had accompanied them during the whole time the Lord Jesus lived among them, beginning from John’s baptism to the day Jesus was taken up.

questions.question: According to Paul's letter to the Romans, what should Christians do instead of being conformed to this world?

options.A: Retreat to the desert to pray
options.C: Be transformed by the renewing of their minds
options.D: Strictly follow the Old Testament laws

questions.explanation: Romans 12:2 admonishes believers: 'Do not conform to the pattern of this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind. Then you will be able to test and approve what God’s will is—his good, pleasing and perfect will.'

questions.question: In the letter of James, how does he describe faith without works?
questions.explanation: James 2:17 states, 'In the same way, faith by itself, if it is not accompanied by action, is dead.' James emphasizes that true faith must manifest in practical deeds.

questions.question: What was God's primary instruction to Abram when He called him from Haran?

options.A: To build an altar in Canaan
options.B: To go to the land He would show him
options.C: To lead his people out of Egypt

questions.explanation: In Genesis 12:1, God tells Abram to 'Go from your country, your people and your father’s household to the land I will show you.' This act of faith required Abraham to leave his familiar surroundings for an unknown destination.

questions.question: Why did God reject Saul as King of Israel?

options.B: Because he consulted a medium in Endor
options.C: Because he failed to carry out the total destruction of the Amalekites
options.D: Because he refused to build the Temple

questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 15, God commanded Saul to completely destroy the Amalekites. Saul spared King Agag and the best of the livestock, claiming they were for sacrifice. Samuel told him, 'To obey is better than sacrifice.'

questions.question: In the Lord's Prayer, what petition is made regarding temptation?

options.C: Give us strength to avoid temptation

questions.explanation: In the model prayer provided in Matthew 6:13, Jesus teaches his disciples to pray: 'And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.'

questions.question: At the miracle of feeding the five thousand, how many baskets of leftovers were collected?
questions.explanation: According to all four Gospels (Matthew 14, Mark 6, Luke 9, John 6), after the people had eaten and were satisfied, the disciples gathered twelve baskets of broken pieces that were left over.

questions.topic: Themes from the Acts of the Apostles
questions.question: What physical ailment did Saul experience immediately after his encounter with Jesus on the road to Damascus?
questions.explanation: In Acts 9:8-9, after the light from heaven flashed around him, Saul got up from the ground, but when he opened his eyes, he could see nothing. He remained blind for three days.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 12, what is the purpose of spiritual gifts given to the church?

options.A: For the personal exaltation of the individual
options.B: For the common good and building up of the church
options.C: To prove who is more holy

questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:7 states, 'Now to each one the manifestation of the Spirit is given for the common good.' Paul emphasizes that gifts are for the benefit of the entire body, not for the individual's vanity.

questions.question: Which prophet was tasked with marrying a prostitute to symbolize God's relationship with unfaithful Israel?
questions.explanation: The book of Hosea begins with God commanding the prophet to marry Gomer, a woman of unfaithfulness. Their tumultuous marriage serves as a living metaphor for God's steadfast love for His unfaithful people, Israel.

questions.question: According to the Beatitudes, who shall see God?

options.D: Those who hunger and thirst for righteousness

questions.explanation: Matthew 5:8 records: 'Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.' This beatitude emphasizes the necessity of inward holiness and sincerity for spiritual intimacy with the Creator.

questions.question: Which two figures from the Old Testament appeared with Jesus on the Mount of Transfiguration?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 17:3, Mark 9:4, and Luke 9:30, Moses (representing the Law) and Elijah (representing the Prophets) appeared and spoke with Jesus about his departure, which he was about to bring to fulfillment at Jerusalem.

questions.topic: Themes from the Acts of the Apostles
questions.question: What was the main decision reached at the Jerusalem Council in Acts 15 regarding Gentile converts?

options.A: They must be circumcised to be saved
options.B: They should avoid food sacrificed to idols, blood, and sexual immorality
options.C: They must offer animal sacrifices in the temple
options.D: They must follow all the laws of Moses

questions.explanation: After much debate, James declared that Gentile Christians should not be burdened with the full yoke of the Law, but should only 'abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals and from sexual immorality.'

questions.question: In the book of Hebrews, faith is defined as the assurance of things hoped for and the conviction of things...?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:1 provides the classic biblical definition of faith: 'Now faith is confidence in what we hope for and assurance about what we do not see.'

questions.question: What did the Israelites eat to sustain them in the wilderness?
questions.explanation: In Exodus 16, God provided manna (a bread-like substance) and quail for the Israelites to eat as they wandered through the desert, demonstrating His provision for their daily needs.

questions.question: For what was King Solomon primarily known when he asked God for wisdom?

options.A: He wanted to defeat his enemies
options.B: He wanted to rule over the people justly
options.C: He wanted to build a large army

questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 3, God asked Solomon what He should give him. Solomon asked for a 'discerning heart to govern your people and to distinguish between right and wrong.'

questions.question: What is the primary lesson of the Parable of the Good Samaritan?

options.A: To show the importance of wealth
options.B: That one's neighbor is anyone in need of mercy
options.C: That priests are more righteous than others
options.D: The history of the Samaritan people

questions.explanation: In Luke 10:25-37, Jesus tells the story to answer the lawyer's question, 'Who is my neighbor?' The parable identifies the neighbor as the one who shows mercy, regardless of social or religious status.

questions.topic: Themes from the Acts of the Apostles
questions.question: On the day of Pentecost, what was the sign that the Holy Spirit had come upon the apostles?

options.B: They saw a vision of angels
options.C: Tongues of fire rested on them
options.D: A star appeared over the house

questions.explanation: Acts 2:3 describes that during Pentecost, 'they saw what seemed to be tongues of fire that separated and came to rest on each of them,' signifying the empowering presence of the Holy Spirit.

questions.question: What does Peter say is the purpose of Christians suffering for doing good?

options.A: Because God likes to test his people
options.C: It is proof that they have sinned
options.D: It serves as a punishment for the world

questions.explanation: In 1 Peter 2:20, Peter writes, 'But how is it to your credit if you receive a beating for doing wrong and endure it? But if you suffer for doing good and you endure it, this is commendable before God.'

questions.question: Which prophet had a vision of a valley of dry bones coming to life?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37 contains the famous vision of the valley of dry bones. God commands the prophet to prophesy over the bones, and they come together and live, symbolizing the spiritual restoration of Israel.

questions.question: Who was the Roman Governor that presided over the trial of Jesus?
questions.explanation: The Gospels consistently identify Pontius Pilate as the Roman Prefect of Judea who oversaw the trial of Jesus and ultimately handed him over to be crucified under pressure from the crowds.

questions.topic: Themes from the Acts of the Apostles
questions.question: Who was the first Christian martyr as recorded in the book of Acts?
questions.explanation: Acts 7 narrates the trial and stoning of Stephen, one of the seven chosen to serve tables. His death made him the first recorded martyr of the Christian Church.

questions.question: What is the 'greatest' of the gifts/virtues mentioned by Paul in 1 Corinthians 13?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:13 concludes the chapter on love: 'And now these three remain: faith, hope and love. But the greatest of these is love.'

questions.question: Why did the prophet Amos condemn the wealthy of Israel?

options.A: For building houses that were too small
options.B: For trampling on the heads of the poor and denying justice to the oppressed
options.C: For not paying their temple taxes
options.D: For living in cities instead of the countryside

questions.explanation: Amos 2:6-7 records the prophet's sharp rebuke: 'They sell the innocent for silver, and the needy for a pair of sandals. They trample on the heads of the poor as on the dust of the ground and deny justice to the oppressed.'

questions.question: Which of these leaders served as the last judge and the first prophet of Israel during the transition to monarchy?
questions.explanation:
### Samuel's Dual Role
**Samuel** occupies a unique position in Israelite history. He acted as the **last of the judges**, governing the people spiritually and judicially, and he was recognized as the **first of the prophets** in the era of the monarchy, anointing both Saul and David.

questions.question: Amos condemned the people of Israel primarily for their lack of:
questions.explanation:
### The Message of Amos
Amos was a prophet of **social justice**. He famously declared that God despised empty rituals (Amos 5:21-24) when they were not accompanied by **righteousness and justice** for the poor and the oppressed in the land.

questions.question: According to the Gospel of Luke, who were the first people to visit the infant Jesus after his birth?
questions.explanation:
### The Nativity Narrative
In Luke 2:8-20, **shepherds** watching their flocks by night were the first to receive the announcement of the birth of the Messiah from the angels and subsequently traveled to Bethlehem to visit the infant Jesus.

questions.question: In his Epistle to the Romans, how does Paul describe the relationship between the Christian and the governing authorities?

options.A: They should rebel against secular laws
options.B: They should be subject to governing authorities
options.C: They should ignore all worldly laws
options.D: They should appoint church members as kings

questions.explanation:
### Romans 13
Paul writes in **Romans 13:1-7** that every person must be **subject to governing authorities**, arguing that authority comes from God and exists to maintain order and punish wrongdoing.

questions.question: Which king of Israel was responsible for the building of the temple, fulfilling his father David's desire?
questions.explanation:
### The Building of the Temple
Although King David prepared the resources for the temple, it was his son, **Solomon**, who oversaw its construction. This accomplishment was a major milestone in Israelite worship (1 Kings 6).

questions.question: Who provided the tomb for the burial of Jesus?
questions.explanation:
### The Burial of Jesus
**Joseph of Arimathea**, a secret disciple of Jesus and a member of the Sanhedrin, boldly asked Pilate for the body of Jesus and laid it in his own newly carved tomb (Matthew 27:57-60).

questions.question: According to Paul's letter to the Corinthians, what is the greatest of all spiritual gifts?
questions.explanation:
### 1 Corinthians 13
Paul devotes the entire 13th chapter of 1 Corinthians to the supremacy of **Love**. He concludes that while prophecy, tongues, and knowledge may cease, love remains the greatest virtue and gift.

questions.question: Where did God first appear to Moses in the burning bush?
questions.explanation:
### The Burning Bush
In Exodus 3, Moses encountered the Lord in a burning bush on **Mount Horeb**, often referred to as the Mountain of God, while tending the flocks of his father-in-law, Jethro.

questions.question: In the Parable of the Sower, what do the thorns represent?
questions.explanation:
### Interpretation of the Sower
In Jesus' explanation of the Parable of the Sower (Matthew 13), the seed that fell among **thorns** represents those who hear the word but are choked by the **cares and wealth of this world**, preventing them from bearing fruit.

questions.question: In the Epistle to the Ephesians, the church is metaphorically compared to what?
questions.explanation:
### Ecclesiology in Ephesians
Paul frequently uses the metaphor of the **Body of Christ** to describe the church in Ephesians 4, emphasizing unity, diversity of gifts, and Christ as the head of the church.

questions.question: Which king of Judah was known for finding the Book of the Law in the temple and instituting major reforms?
questions.explanation:
### Josiah's Reform
**King Josiah** (2 Kings 22) initiated a great religious reform after the High Priest Hilkiah discovered the Book of the Law (likely Deuteronomy) during temple repairs, leading to the removal of idols throughout Judah.

questions.question: What miracle did Jesus perform by walking on the water?

options.C: Walking on the Sea of Galilee

questions.explanation:
### Jesus Walks on Water
Walking on the water is one of the distinct miracles found in the Synoptic Gospels (and John), demonstrating Jesus' power over the forces of nature, specifically the **Sea of Galilee**.

questions.question: James 2:17 states that faith without works is:
questions.explanation:
### Faith and Works
The Epistle of James emphasizes the practical application of the Christian faith. He famously asserts that **'faith by itself, if it does not have works, is dead'** (James 2:17).

questions.question: How many plagues did God send upon Egypt to persuade Pharaoh to release the Israelites?
questions.explanation:
### The Ten Plagues
God sent **ten distinct plagues** against the Egyptians to demonstrate His sovereignty and to compel Pharaoh to let the children of Israel go, culminating in the death of the firstborn.

questions.question: Who was the first Christian martyr recorded in the Acts of the Apostles?
questions.explanation:
### The Martyrdom of Stephen
**Stephen**, one of the seven chosen to serve the widows in the early church, was stoned to death for his bold testimony, becoming the **first martyr** of the Christian faith (Acts 7).

questions.question: According to 1 Peter, how should Christians respond to persecution?

options.C: With patience and trust in God

questions.explanation:
### Suffering for Christ
1 Peter encourages believers to endure suffering with **patience and dignity**, modeling their behavior after Christ, who suffered unjustly but did not revile in return (1 Peter 2:21-23).

questions.question: Prophet Isaiah compared the coming Messiah to a 'Suffering Servant' in which chapter?
questions.explanation:
### The Suffering Servant
**Isaiah 53** is the fourth of the 'Servant Songs' in Isaiah. It provides a vivid description of the Messiah as one who would be despised, rejected, and pierced for our transgressions, foretelling his sacrifice.

questions.question: What was Matthew's profession before he was called by Jesus to be a disciple?
questions.explanation:
### Matthew's Calling
Matthew (also called Levi) was a **tax collector** at a custom house in Capernaum before Jesus called him to follow Him (Matthew 9:9).

questions.question: Paul, in his letter to the Galatians, lists the 'Fruit of the Spirit'. Which of these is NOT on that list?
questions.explanation:
### The Fruit of the Spirit
Found in Galatians 5:22-23, the list includes love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control. **Eloquence** is not included in the biblical list.

questions.question: Which judge led the Israelites to victory over the Midianites with a small army of only 300 men?
questions.explanation:
### Gideon's Victory
**Gideon** famously tested God with a fleece and later reduced his army from 32,000 to **300 men**, whom God used to miraculously defeat the Midianite army using trumpets and torches (Judges 7).

questions.question: Jesus taught that the Kingdom of God is like which of these small objects, representing its growth?
questions.explanation:
### The Mustard Seed
In the Parable of the Mustard Seed (Matthew 13:31-32), Jesus describes the Kingdom of God as being like a **mustard seed**, which, though the smallest of seeds, grows into a tree large enough for birds to nest in.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 15, what does Paul argue would be the case if Christ had not been raised?

options.B: We would still have to observe the Mosaic Law
options.D: The apostles would still have authority

questions.explanation:
### The Importance of the Resurrection
Paul presents a powerful apologetic for the Resurrection, stating that if Christ has not been raised, preaching is vain, and the **faith of the believers is empty** and futile (1 Corinthians 15:14).

questions.question: Which prophet was taken up to heaven in a whirlwind?
questions.explanation:
### The Translation of Elijah
In 2 Kings 2, **Elijah** did not die in the conventional sense but was taken up into heaven in a chariot of fire by a whirlwind, leaving his mantle to his successor, Elisha.

questions.question: At the Council of Jerusalem, what was the primary decision regarding the Gentile converts?

options.B: They should not be burdened with the full Law of Moses
options.C: They were excluded from the church

questions.explanation:
### The Council of Jerusalem
The Council of Jerusalem (Acts 15) resolved that Gentile converts were not required to observe the entire Mosaic Law, specifically circumcision, but were asked to abstain from certain practices like eating food sacrificed to idols.

questions.question: In the letter to the Ephesians, what does Paul describe as the 'armor of God'?

options.B: Spiritual tools like the shield of faith and the sword of the spirit
options.C: The teachings of the twelve apostles only
options.D: The laws of the Roman Empire

questions.explanation:
### The Armor of God
Paul uses the imagery of Roman military gear to describe the **spiritual armor** required for the Christian's struggle against spiritual forces, including the breastplate of righteousness and the helmet of salvation (Ephesians 6:10-18).

questions.question: Who was the first woman mentioned in the Creation story?
questions.explanation:
### The First Woman
According to the Genesis narrative, **Eve** was created by God from the rib of Adam to be his companion and helper, becoming the first woman.

questions.question: Which of Jesus' disciples betrayed him to the chief priests?
questions.explanation:
### The Betrayal
**Judas Iscariot**, one of the twelve disciples, conspired with the chief priests and agreed to betray Jesus for thirty pieces of silver, identifying him with a kiss in Gethsemane.

questions.question: What is the primary emphasis of the letter to the Colossians?

options.B: The collection for the poor in Jerusalem
options.C: The structure of the church office
options.D: The history of the Jewish people

questions.explanation:
### The Supremacy of Christ
The central theme of Colossians is the **supremacy and sufficiency of Christ**. Paul argues that Christ is the image of the invisible God and that in Him dwells the fullness of the Godhead.

questions.question: Which mountain did Moses ascend to receive the Ten Commandments?
questions.explanation:
### The Ten Commandments
After the departure from Egypt, Moses ascended **Mount Sinai**, where God descended in fire and gave him the Ten Commandments written on two tablets of stone (Exodus 20).

questions.question: What is the 'Great Commission' found at the end of the Gospel of Matthew?

options.B: To go and make disciples of all nations
options.C: To keep the Jewish Sabbath holy
options.D: To build a church in Rome

questions.explanation:
### The Great Commission
In Matthew 28:19-20, Jesus gives his final instructions to the disciples, commanding them to **'go and make disciples of all nations'**, baptizing them and teaching them to obey everything he commanded.

questions.question: In the account of creation, what does the 'Spirit of God' hovering over the waters signify?

options.B: The creative and life-giving power of God
options.C: The separation of day and night
options.D: The existence of water before the earth

questions.explanation: In Genesis 1:2, the 'Spirit of God' (Ruach Elohim) signifies the active, sovereign power of God that brings order out of chaos. It represents the divine presence and agency in the creative process.

questions.question: Which of these was NOT a consequence of the Fall for Adam and Eve?

options.B: Eating by the sweat of the brow

questions.explanation: Genesis 3 details the curses: toil for man, pain for the woman, and spiritual separation. Total annihilation (non-existence) is not mentioned; rather, humanity experienced spiritual death and physical decay.

questions.question: Abraham's call from God involved leaving his kindred. What does this primarily demonstrate?

options.B: Total reliance and submission to God's providence
options.C: A desire to escape from local enemies

questions.explanation: Abraham's departure from Ur was an act of faith (Hebrews 11:8). It signifies total trust in God’s promise over earthly security and ancestral ties.

questions.question: Why did God tell Moses to remove his sandals at the burning bush?

options.A: To prevent damage to the holy ground
options.B: Because the place was holy ground
options.D: As a sign of ritual cleansing

questions.explanation: Exodus 3:5 explicitly states, 'Do not come any closer... Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy ground,' emphasizing the sanctity of God's presence.

questions.question: The first four commandments of the Decalogue are primarily concerned with:

options.B: The relationship between man and God
options.D: Civil laws for the nation of Israel

questions.explanation: The first four commandments deal specifically with worship, the nature of God, idolatry, and keeping the Sabbath, defining the vertical relationship between the Creator and the created.

questions.question: What primary reason did Samuel give for the rejection of Saul as king?

options.B: Saul's failure to wait for the prophet's sacrifice
options.D: Saul's reluctance to lead the people

questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 13, Saul disobeyed the divine command by usurping the priestly role and offering the sacrifice himself, demonstrating a lack of faith and obedience to God's set procedures.

questions.question: Amos criticized the people of Israel most severely for:

options.B: Oppression of the poor and the perversion of justice
options.D: Refusal to pay taxes to the king

questions.explanation: Amos was a prophet of social justice. He condemned the rich for trampling the heads of the poor into the dust and turning justice into wormwood (Amos 5:7, 2:7).

questions.question: What was Jeremiah's metaphor regarding the 'New Covenant'?

options.C: Laws kept in the Ark of the Covenant

questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:33 foretells the New Covenant: 'I will put my law in their minds and write it on their hearts,' contrasting it with the stone tablets of the old law.

questions.question: What is the central theme of the Book of Ecclesiastes?

options.B: The vanity of life apart from God

questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes explores the meaning of life, concluding that all worldly pursuits are 'hebel' (vanity) unless anchored in the fear and obedience of God.

questions.question: Which temptation of Jesus involved the misuse of power for personal sustenance?

options.B: Throwing himself from the temple pinnacle
options.C: Worshiping Satan for the kingdoms of the world

questions.explanation: The first temptation (Matthew 4:3) challenged Jesus to use his divine power to satisfy his physical hunger, which he refused by quoting scripture.

questions.question: According to the Beatitudes, who shall see God?
questions.explanation: Matthew 5:8 states, 'Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God,' highlighting the necessity of inward holiness.

questions.question: In the Parable of the Sower, the seed falling among thorns represents:

options.A: Those who fall away due to lack of depth
options.B: Those who are persecuted for the Word
options.C: Those who hear the Word but are choked by worldly cares
options.D: Those who do not hear the Word at all

questions.explanation: Jesus explains that thorns represent the anxieties of life and the deceitfulness of wealth, which choke the Word, rendering it unfruitful (Matthew 13:22).

questions.question: What did Peter's confession ('You are the Christ') immediately precede in Mark 8?

options.B: The miracle of the feeding of the five thousand
options.C: The first prediction of Jesus' passion

questions.explanation: After Peter's declaration of faith, Jesus immediately began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected (Mark 8:31).

questions.subtopic: The Coming of the Holy Spirit
questions.question: What did the phenomenon of 'tongues of fire' represent at Pentecost?

options.A: The destruction of the Jewish Temple
options.B: The empowerment and purification of the apostles
options.C: A sign of the coming judgment
options.D: A test for the crowd gathered in Jerusalem

questions.explanation: The fire represents the presence of God (theophany) and the refining power of the Holy Spirit, which enabled the apostles to preach boldly.

questions.question: To whom was Saul traveling when he encountered the resurrected Christ?
questions.explanation: Saul was on the road to Damascus to persecute Christians when he was blinded by a light and heard the voice of Jesus (Acts 9).

questions.question: What was the main outcome of the Jerusalem Council (Acts 15)?

options.A: Gentiles must follow all Jewish laws
options.B: Gentiles need only abstain from idolatry and immorality
options.C: Jewish Christians should stop observing the Torah
options.D: The apostles would move to Rome

questions.explanation: The Council concluded that Gentiles should not be burdened with the full weight of the Mosaic Law, but should avoid specific practices like eating meat sacrificed to idols or sexual immorality.

questions.question: Peter’s vision of the sheet of animals taught him that:

options.A: He should only eat clean animals
options.B: The Gentiles were also included in the Gospel plan
options.D: He should stop preaching to the Jews

questions.explanation: The vision in Acts 10 was God's way of showing Peter that the Gospel was no longer restricted to Jews; 'what God has cleansed, you must not call common.'

questions.question: Which of these was a primary charge brought against Jesus before Pilate?

options.A: Refusal to pay taxes to Caesar
options.B: Claiming to be the King of the Jews

questions.explanation: The political charge brought by the Jewish leaders to Pilate was that Jesus claimed to be 'King of the Jews,' which was considered sedition against Rome.

questions.question: Which woman was the first to see the risen Jesus in the accounts of the Gospels?
questions.explanation: All four Gospels identify Mary Magdalene as one of the first, or the very first, to encounter the resurrected Christ at the tomb.

questions.question: What is the core argument of James regarding faith?

options.A: Faith is sufficient regardless of deeds
options.C: Works are only for the apostles
options.D: Faith is a private mental exercise

questions.explanation: James 2:17 states, 'faith by itself, if it does not have works, is dead,' arguing that true faith must manifest in character and action.

questions.question: How does 1 Peter advise believers to respond to suffering?

options.B: By enduring it patiently and keeping a clear conscience
options.D: By offering bribes to the authorities

questions.explanation: 1 Peter teaches that suffering for righteousness' sake is a privilege that aligns the believer with Christ's sufferings, requiring endurance and holiness.

questions.question: In Romans, what does Paul describe as the 'wages of sin'?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:23 states, 'For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.'

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 12, what is the purpose of spiritual gifts?

options.B: Building up the body of Christ

questions.explanation: Paul emphasizes that gifts are given for the 'common good' and the edification (building up) of the entire church body.

questions.question: According to 1 John, what is the evidence that one has passed from death to life?
questions.explanation: 1 John 3:14: 'We know that we have passed out of death into life, because we love the brothers. Whoever does not love abides in death.'

questions.question: Why did Paul rebuke Peter in Antioch (Galatians 2)?

options.A: Peter was eating with the Gentiles
options.B: Peter separated himself from Gentiles due to fear of the circumcision party

questions.explanation: Paul confronted Peter because he withdrew from table fellowship with Gentiles after men from James arrived, which compromised the Gospel of grace.

questions.question: Hebrews 11 defines faith as:

options.B: The substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen
options.C: A logical conclusion based on historical evidence

questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:1 provides the classic biblical definition of faith as confidence in what we hope for and assurance about what we do not see.

questions.question: In 1 Thessalonians, what is the primary encouragement Paul gives regarding those who have died before Christ's return?

options.B: They will rise first at the sound of the trumpet
options.D: They remain unconscious until the end

questions.explanation: Paul clarifies in 1 Thessalonians 4 that those who have 'fallen asleep' in Christ will not be disadvantaged but will rise first when the Lord returns.

questions.question: In Ephesians 6, what is described as the 'sword of the Spirit'?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 6:17 identifies the sword of the Spirit as the Word of God, which is the offensive weapon for the Christian in spiritual warfare.

questions.question: What is the basis for Christian submission to governing authorities in Romans 13?

options.B: Recognition that all authority is ordained by God
options.C: To gain favor from the state
options.D: Because the state is always right

questions.explanation: Paul argues that because all authority is established by God, Christians should be subject to governing powers as a matter of conscience.

questions.question: What does Paul identify as his 'thorn in the flesh'?

options.B: A messenger of Satan intended to keep him humble

questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 12:7, Paul mentions the 'thorn' and notes that it was given to prevent him from becoming conceited due to the abundance of his revelations.

questions.question: According to Genesis 1, what was created on the fourth day to govern the day and the night?
questions.explanation:
### Explanation
According to the Genesis creation account (Genesis 1:14-19), God created the celestial bodies—the **sun, moon, and stars**—on the fourth day. Their purpose was to separate light from darkness and act as signs for seasons, days, and years.

questions.question: Where did God first command Abram to leave his country and kindred?
questions.explanation:
### Explanation
In Genesis 12:1-3, God gave the initial command to Abram while he was still in **Ur of the Chaldeans**. Although Abram moved to Haran with his father Terah, the original calling originated from his homeland, Ur.

questions.question: Who was left in charge of the Israelites when Moses went up Mount Sinai to receive the Ten Commandments?
questions.explanation:
### Explanation
In Exodus 24:14, before ascending the mountain, Moses instructed the elders, specifically **Aaron and Hur**, to remain in charge of the people. However, Aaron is specifically noted for his failure to restrain the people from idolatry during Moses' absence.

questions.question: Where did Elijah hide during the drought he prophesied against Ahab?
questions.explanation:
### Explanation
Following his confrontation with Ahab, God commanded Elijah in 1 Kings 17:3 to turn eastward and hide by the **Brook Cherith**, which is east of the Jordan, where he was fed by ravens.

questions.question: Amos condemned the people of Israel primarily for their lack of which virtue?
questions.explanation:
### Explanation
Amos is famously known as the 'prophet of social justice.' In Amos 5:24, he states: 'But let justice roll down like waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream.' He criticized the elite for oppressing the poor despite their religious activities.

questions.question: What was the immediate cause of the rebellion of Absalom against his father, David?

options.C: David's refusal to fight the Philistines
options.D: A dispute over the succession to the throne

questions.explanation:
### Explanation
Absalom’s resentment grew after his brother Amnon raped his sister, Tamar. When David failed to punish Amnon, Absalom took matters into his own hands by killing Amnon and eventually staging a coup to seize the throne (2 Samuel 13-15).

questions.question: According to the Book of Proverbs, what is the beginning of wisdom?
questions.explanation:
### Explanation
Proverbs 9:10 explicitly states: 'The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom, and the knowledge of the Holy One is insight.'

questions.question: Who was the king who granted Nehemiah permission to return to Jerusalem to rebuild its walls?
questions.explanation:
### Explanation
Nehemiah served as a cupbearer to King **Artaxerxes I** of Persia. In Nehemiah 2, the king noticed Nehemiah's sadness and granted him the authority and materials to return to Judah to rebuild Jerusalem.

questions.question: In the Gospel of Luke, who were the first to hear the news of Jesus' birth from the angels?
questions.explanation:
### Explanation
According to Luke 2:8-12, an angel of the Lord appeared to **shepherds** abiding in the field, keeping watch over their flock by night, to announce the birth of the Savior.

questions.question: How did Jesus counter the devil's temptation to turn stones into bread?

options.B: By quoting the book of Deuteronomy
options.C: By fasting for another forty days

questions.explanation:
### Explanation
In Matthew 4:4, Jesus responded to the temptation by quoting Deuteronomy 8:3: 'Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God.'

questions.question: What prompted Jesus to calm the storm on the Sea of Galilee?

options.D: Jesus' desire to demonstrate authority over nature

questions.explanation:
### Explanation
After calming the storm, Jesus rebuked his disciples, asking, 'Why are you so afraid? Have you still no faith?' (Mark 4:40). Their fear highlighted their lack of trust in His divine presence.

questions.question: During the Last Supper, what did Jesus say the cup of wine represented?

options.B: The joy of the coming kingdom
options.C: The sacrifice of the Passover lamb
options.D: The forgiveness of sins through repentance

questions.explanation:
### Explanation
In Matthew 26:27-28, Jesus took the cup, gave thanks, and said, 'Drink from it, all of you, for this is my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.'

questions.question: On the day of Pentecost, what sign accompanied the coming of the Holy Spirit upon the apostles?

options.C: A bright light in the sky

questions.explanation:
### Explanation
Acts 2:3 describes the event where 'divided tongues as of fire appeared to them and rested on each one of them,' signaling the descent of the Holy Spirit.

questions.question: Who was the first Christian martyr recorded in the Acts of the Apostles?
questions.explanation:
### Explanation
Stephen, one of the seven deacons chosen to serve the church, was stoned to death after his defense before the Sanhedrin, making him the first recorded Christian martyr in Acts 7.

questions.question: What was the name of the man sent by God to pray for Paul to regain his sight in Damascus?
questions.explanation:
### Explanation
As recorded in Acts 9:10-17, the Lord spoke to **Ananias** in a vision, instructing him to go to the house of Judas on Straight Street to lay hands on Saul of Tarsus so he could receive his sight and be filled with the Holy Spirit.

questions.question: In the book of Romans, Paul argues that justification comes through what?

options.D: Keeping the traditions of the elders

questions.explanation:
### Explanation
Paul’s central thesis in Romans (e.g., Romans 3:28) is that a person is justified by **faith** apart from the works of the law, emphasizing grace as the foundation of salvation.

questions.question: According to 1 Peter, how should Christians respond to persecution?

options.B: By rejoicing in their participation in Christ's sufferings

questions.explanation:
### Explanation
1 Peter 4:13 encourages believers to 'rejoice insofar as you share Christ's sufferings, that you may also rejoice and be glad when his glory is revealed.'

questions.question: James states that 'faith without works is...'?
questions.explanation:
### Explanation
James 2:26 provides the famous conclusion: 'For as the body apart from the spirit is dead, so also faith apart from works is dead.'

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 13, which of the following is considered the 'greatest' of the spiritual gifts/virtues?
questions.explanation:
### Explanation
Paul concludes the famous 'love chapter' in 1 Corinthians 13:13 by stating, 'So now faith, hope, and love abide, these three; but the greatest of these is love.'

questions.question: What was Paul's primary request to Philemon regarding Onesimus?

options.B: To receive him back no longer as a slave but as a beloved brother
options.D: To give him a position of leadership in the church

questions.explanation:
### Explanation
In the letter to Philemon, Paul asks Philemon to welcome back his runaway slave, Onesimus, treating him not as a servant but as a 'beloved brother' in the Lord, reflecting the transforming power of the Gospel on social relations.

questions.question: Why did God reject Saul as king of Israel?

options.A: He failed to build the Temple
options.B: He disobeyed God's command regarding the Amalekites

questions.explanation:
### Explanation
In 1 Samuel 15, Saul failed to utterly destroy the Amalekites and their livestock, keeping the best for himself. Samuel declared that because Saul rejected the word of the Lord, the Lord had rejected him as king.

questions.question: What message did the marriage of Hosea to Gomer symbolize?

options.A: The necessity of marriage for prophets
options.B: God's unconditional love for unfaithful Israel
options.D: The need for stricter law enforcement

questions.explanation:
### Explanation
God commanded Hosea to marry a woman of whoredom to symbolize the spiritual adultery of Israel, who had forsaken God for idols. Hosea’s persistence in seeking his unfaithful wife represented God’s persistent love for His people.

questions.question: In the Parable of the Prodigal Son, what did the older brother do when he heard of his brother's return?

options.A: He welcomed him with open arms
options.B: He was angry and refused to go in
options.D: He went to fetch the fatted calf

questions.explanation:
### Explanation
According to Luke 15:28, the older brother was filled with resentment and refused to celebrate the return of his brother, showing his lack of compassion and his own legalistic heart.

questions.question: Who was the first Gentile to receive the Holy Spirit after Peter preached to him?
questions.explanation:
### Explanation
In Acts 10, Peter is sent to the house of **Cornelius**, a Roman centurion. As Peter spoke, the Holy Spirit fell upon all who heard the word, proving that salvation was also for the Gentiles.

questions.question: Paul accuses the Galatians of falling under a curse because they were following what?

options.B: The heresy of Judaizers who insisted on circumcision

questions.explanation:
### Explanation
In Galatians 3:1-3, Paul strongly rebukes the Galatians for turning back to the Law, specifically the insistence of the Judaizers that Gentile converts must be circumcised to be saved.

questions.question: Which judge was known for his extreme physical strength?
questions.explanation:
### Explanation
Samson, as a Nazirite, was granted supernatural strength by the Spirit of the Lord, which he used to fight the Philistines as described in Judges 13–16.

questions.question: According to the Sermon on the Mount, who does Jesus say are 'blessed' because they shall be called sons of God?
questions.explanation:
### Explanation
In the Beatitudes (Matthew 5:9), Jesus declares: 'Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called sons of God.'

questions.question: How does 1 Peter describe the Christian community in relation to the world?
questions.explanation:
### Explanation
1 Peter 2:11 addresses Christians as 'sojourners and exiles,' emphasizing that their citizenship is in heaven and they should abstain from worldly passions.

questions.question: Where were the disciples first called 'Christians'?
questions.explanation:
### Explanation
Acts 11:26 states: 'And in Antioch the disciples were for the first time called Christians.' This was a major center for the early Gentile church.

questions.question: What was the main argument of Job's three friends?

options.B: That suffering is always a result of personal sin
options.C: That Job should curse God and die

questions.explanation:
### Explanation
Job’s friends (Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar) held the traditional view that God always rewards the righteous and punishes the wicked, therefore implying that Job’s great suffering was evidence of secret, unconfessed sin.

questions.question: Which of these events in the life of Jonah best illustrates God's sovereignty over nature?

options.A: The appointment of a fish to swallow Jonah
options.B: Jonah's attempt to flee to Tarshish
options.C: The casting of lots by the sailors
options.D: Jonah's refusal to preach in Nineveh

questions.explanation: God's sovereignty is portrayed through His control over the elements and creatures. In the Book of Jonah, God 'appointed' a great fish to swallow Jonah (Jonah 1:17), demonstrating that even the forces of nature are at His command to execute His sovereign will.

questions.question: Amos was specifically told by Amaziah to flee to which location?
questions.explanation: In Amos 7:12, Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, commanded Amos to flee to the land of Judah to earn his living by prophesying there, as he did not want Amos to prophesy at the King's sanctuary in Bethel.

questions.question: According to the synoptic gospels, what was the sign that accompanied the baptism of Jesus?

options.B: The heavens opening and the Spirit descending like a dove
options.C: A blinding light appearing to the crowd

questions.explanation: Matthew 3:16-17, Mark 1:10-11, and Luke 3:21-22 all record that as Jesus came out of the water, the heavens opened, and the Spirit of God descended like a dove, followed by a voice from heaven declaring His identity.

questions.question: What was the main criterion for the selection of the seven men to serve the Hellenistic widows in Acts 6?

options.A: They were relatives of the Apostles
options.C: They were of good repute, full of the Spirit and wisdom
options.D: They were the oldest members of the church

questions.explanation: In Acts 6:3, the Apostles instructed the congregation to select seven men 'of good repute, full of the Spirit and of wisdom' to handle the distribution of food, showing that spiritual character was essential for administrative service.

questions.question: In the book of Galatians, to whom does Paul compare the law before the coming of Christ?
questions.explanation: Paul describes the law in Galatians 3:24 as a 'tutor' or 'custodian' (paidagogos) that kept Israel under guard until the faith in Christ was revealed, emphasizing the transition from the law to grace.

questions.question: Why did God reject Saul as King of Israel?

options.B: He failed to completely destroy the Amalekites
options.C: He lost the war against the Philistines
options.D: He refused to marry his daughter to David

questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 15, Saul disobeyed the Lord's instruction to completely destroy Amalek and their property. He spared Agag and the best of the livestock, leading Samuel to declare that God had rejected him as king for his disobedience.

questions.question: What does the 'seed' represent in the Parable of the Sower?

options.C: The money given to the church
options.D: The missionary zeal of the apostles

questions.explanation: In Luke 8:11, Jesus explains the parable by explicitly stating, 'The seed is the word of God.' The soil represents the hearts of the listeners.

questions.question: In Colossians 3, what does Paul urge believers to put on after putting off their old nature?
questions.explanation: Colossians 3:12 provides a list of virtues including compassion, kindness, humility, meekness, and patience, which Christians are encouraged to 'clothe' themselves with as a reflection of their new life in Christ.

questions.question: What major item was discovered during the temple renovation under King Josiah?
questions.explanation: During the repair of the temple in 2 Kings 22:8, Hilkiah the high priest found the 'Book of the Law' in the house of the Lord, which led to a national renewal and religious reform under Josiah.

questions.question: Where did Peter perform the miracle of raising Tabitha (Dorcas) from the dead?
questions.explanation: In Acts 9:36-42, Peter went to Joppa where Tabitha, a disciple known for her good works, had died. Through prayer, Peter raised her back to life.

questions.question: In 1 Peter, how should Christians react to suffering?

options.B: By enduring it patiently and doing good
options.C: By running away from the community

questions.explanation: 1 Peter 2:20-21 emphasizes that if a believer suffers for doing good and endures it, it is commendable before God, as Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example.

questions.question: When God called Jeremiah, what was his initial response regarding his qualification?

options.B: He was only a youth and could not speak
options.C: He was not of the priestly lineage
options.D: He lacked the courage to face the King

questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 1:6, Jeremiah protested his calling by saying, 'Ah, Lord God! Behold, I do not know how to speak, for I am only a youth.' God reassured him by touching his mouth.

questions.question: Which two Old Testament figures appeared with Jesus during the Transfiguration?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 17:3, Mark 9:4, and Luke 9:30, Moses (representing the Law) and Elijah (representing the Prophets) appeared and spoke with Jesus about His departure.

questions.question: According to Galatians 5, which of these is NOT listed as a fruit of the Spirit?
questions.explanation: The fruit of the Spirit listed in Galatians 5:22-23 includes love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control. 'Eloquence' is not listed.

questions.question: What was the primary reason given by the prophets for the Babylonian exile?
questions.explanation: The prophets consistently warned that the exile was a divine judgment resulting from Israel's breach of the covenant, specifically through idolatry and social injustice.

questions.question: What was the final decision of the Jerusalem Council regarding Gentile converts?

options.B: They should abstain from things polluted by idols, blood, and things strangled
options.C: They must follow the entire Law of Moses
options.D: They must offer animal sacrifices in Jerusalem

questions.explanation: Acts 15:20, 29 records that the council decided not to burden Gentiles with the law of circumcision but requested they abstain from food offered to idols, blood, and sexual immorality.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 15, what does Paul argue would be the case if Christ had not been raised?

options.A: Our faith would still be valid
options.B: Our preaching and faith would be in vain
options.C: We would still be saved by the Law
options.D: Only the disciples would be affected

questions.explanation: Paul argues in 1 Corinthians 15:14 that the entire basis of the Christian faith rests on the resurrection. Without it, the gospel message is pointless and believers are still in their sins.

questions.question: What did Solomon ask God for when he was offered anything he desired?

options.C: An understanding mind to govern the people

questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 3:9, Solomon asked for an 'understanding mind' (wisdom) to discern between good and evil so that he might effectively govern the people of Israel.

questions.question: What was the final temptation of Jesus in the wilderness according to Matthew?

options.B: To throw Himself down from the pinnacle of the temple
options.C: To worship Satan in exchange for the kingdoms of the world
options.D: To call for angels to save Him

questions.explanation: In Matthew 4:8-9, the third temptation involves the devil taking Jesus to a high mountain, showing Him all the kingdoms of the world, and asking for worship in exchange for authority over them.

questions.question: According to 1 John, what is the clearest evidence that one loves God?
questions.explanation: 1 John 5:3 emphasizes that 'this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments.' Obedience is presented as the primary metric of true love for God.

questions.question: The Passover feast was instituted to commemorate what event?

options.A: The giving of the Ten Commandments
options.B: The liberation of the Israelites from slavery in Egypt

questions.explanation: The Passover (Exodus 12) was established to mark the night the Lord 'passed over' the houses of the Israelites, sparing their firstborn and facilitating their departure from Egyptian bondage.

questions.question: What happened to Saul immediately after he encountered the risen Christ on the road to Damascus?

options.B: He was blinded for three days
options.C: He started preaching in the synagogues
options.D: He returned to Jerusalem to report to the Apostles

questions.explanation: Acts 9:8-9 records that after the light from heaven flashed around him, Saul rose, but could not see anything, and remained without sight for three days until Ananias visited him.

questions.question: Which Old Testament figure does James use as an example of faith working with works?
questions.explanation: James 2:21-23 points to Abraham, who was justified by works when he offered his son Isaac upon the altar, arguing that his faith was made complete by his actions.

questions.question: What was Nehemiah’s primary mission when he returned to Jerusalem?

options.B: To rebuild the wall of Jerusalem

questions.explanation: Nehemiah 2:17-18 details Nehemiah's burden for the ruined walls of Jerusalem. His leadership enabled the Jews to rebuild the walls despite significant opposition from surrounding enemies.

questions.subtopic: The Parable of the Prodigal Son
questions.question: In the Parable of the Prodigal Son, why did the younger son decide to return home?

options.A: He was forced by the authorities
options.B: He realized his father was wealthy
options.C: He suffered from severe hunger and realized he could work for his father

questions.explanation: Luke 15:17 describes how the son, in the midst of famine and misery, 'came to himself' and remembered his father’s servants had plenty of food, prompting his return.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 12, what is the ultimate goal of the distribution of spiritual gifts?

options.A: To prove one is holier than others
options.B: For the common good of the church
options.C: To attain individual status in the ministry

questions.explanation: Paul clarifies in 1 Corinthians 12:7 that 'to each is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the common good,' emphasizing the unity of the body of Christ over individual exhibition.

questions.question: What was the sign of the covenant between God and Noah?
questions.explanation: In Genesis 9:13, God set the rainbow in the clouds as a token (sign) of the covenant between Him and the earth, guaranteeing that He would never again destroy all flesh by flood.

questions.question: Who did Philip encounter on the road from Jerusalem to Gaza?
questions.explanation: Acts 8:26-39 recounts Philip's encounter with the Ethiopian eunuch, a court official of the Queen of the Ethiopians, whom Philip baptized after explaining the passage in Isaiah.

questions.question: In 1 Thessalonians 4, what is the main purpose of Paul’s teaching on the return of the Lord?

options.A: To incite fear in the sinners
options.B: To provide comfort and hope to the believers
options.C: To establish a specific date for the event

questions.explanation: Paul concludes his teaching on the return of Christ in 1 Thessalonians 4:18 by saying, 'Therefore encourage one another with these words,' highlighting that the doctrine is intended to bring comfort, not terror.
